abstract: Choriocarcinoma of the colon presented as life-threatening lower gastrointestinal bleeding and a pathologic femoral fracture in a 42-year-old man. Elevated serum carcinoembryonic antigen (CEA) levels and immunohistochemical positivity for CEA in neoplastic syncytiotrophoblasts were noted, as well as the expected positivity for the beta subunit of human chorionic gonadotropin (beta HCG). Additional cases, including one of two gestational choriocarcinomas and one of four testicular choriocarcinomas studied immunocytochemically for CEA also demonstrated positivity. Although CEA staining is commonly associated with tumors derived from the surface epithelium of the gastrointestinal tract and other organs, its presence in choriocarcinomas should not be interpreted as conclusive evidence of primary origin from these sites.
abstract_ja: 42歳男性の大腸絨毛癌が、下部消化管出血と病的大腿骨骨折を呈して発症した。血清CEA値の上昇と、腫瘍性合胞体栄養膜細胞におけるCEAの免疫組織化学的陽性が認められ、β-hCGサブユニットの陽性も確認された。妊娠性絨毛癌2例中1例、精巣絨毛癌4例中1例についてもCEAを免疫細胞化学的に検討したところ、同様に陽性であった。CEA染色は一般に消化管などの表層上皮由来の腫瘍でみられるが、絨毛癌におけるCEA陽性は、これらの臓器が原発であることの決定的な証拠とみなすべきではない。
